title: Trump Declares Deal 'Largely Negotiated' on Truth Social — Simultaneously Tells Axios '50/50'; 5th Round of US-Iran Rome Talks Ends Without Final Breakthrough — Day 85
detail: President Trump posted on Truth Social on May 23, 2026 (Day 85) that 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries,' promising the 'final aspects and details' would be announced 'shortly.' The statement sent diplomatic circles into a frenzy, with markets responding strongly to deal optimism. However, in a near-simultaneous conversation with Axios, Trump conceded there was a '50/50' chance of a deal versus 'blow[ing] them to kingdom come' — a stark admission of uncertainty that dampened immediate euphoria. The 5th round of US-Iran talks, held that day in Rome under Pakistani and Omani facilitation, ended without a final breakthrough. Both sides described the session as 'constructive' and confirmed they would continue negotiations. Trump also held a call that day with leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan, Jordan, Egypt, and the UAE to coordinate regional support for the emerging framework. VP Vance and envoy Steve Witkoff participated in the call. The dual messaging — optimism on Truth Social, uncertainty to Axios — reflected the genuine ambiguity of a negotiation still hinging on the nuclear moratorium duration and Hormuz control questions.

media.caption: Day 85: Trump declares US-Iran deal 'largely negotiated' on Truth Social — simultaneously tells Axios there is a '50/50' chance of deal or new strikes

title: Pakistan Army Chief Munir Completes 'Short But Highly Productive' Tehran Visit — Interior Minister Naqvi Also Arrives; Both Sides Report 'Encouraging' Progress — Day 85
detail: Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir concluded a 'short but highly productive' visit to Tehran on May 23, 2026 (Day 85), reversing the May 22 cancellation. Munir met with Iranian President Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Araghchi, and Interior Minister Momeni. Both Pakistan and Iran publicly described the visit as yielding 'encouraging' progress toward a final understanding — the most positive bilateral signal since the April 8 ceasefire. Simultaneously, Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran for a two-day visit (his third trip in one week), conducting parallel tracks of negotiations at the ministerial level alongside Munir's general-officer track. The dual-track Pakistani mediation — army chief meeting security officials, interior minister meeting civilian counterparts — reflects Pakistan's comprehensive engagement strategy. The 'encouraging' characterization from Islamabad and Tehran was notably stronger than Rubio's 'good signs' and 'slight progress' language from May 22. Iran, US, and Pakistan all publicly confirmed on May 23 that 'progress' had been made, the first trilateral public acknowledgment of progress in the same news cycle.

media.caption: Day 85: Pakistan Army Chief Munir completes 'highly productive' Tehran visit — Interior Minister Naqvi also arrives; trilateral US-Iran-Pakistan progress acknowledged

title: IDF Strikes Hezbollah Underground Weapons Site in Beqaa Valley; Lebanese Army Soldier Wounded Near Nabatieh — Ceasefire Continues to Fray — Day 85
detail: Israeli airstrikes hit a Hezbollah underground weapons production site in the Beqaa Valley and additional Hezbollah infrastructure in the Tyre area on May 23, 2026 (Day 85). The IDF said advance evacuation warnings were issued before both strikes. A Lebanese army soldier was wounded when the IDF struck a vehicle near Nabatieh that had departed a Hezbollah-linked site — IDF stated it identified the vehicle as 'driving suspiciously' from a Hezbollah compound. Air-raid sirens sounded in the Israeli northern communities of Shtula and Shlomi due to drone infiltration warnings from Lebanon. The overnight strikes mark the IDF's continued operations under the 45-day Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension (announced May 16), which technically requires Hezbollah disarmament and IDF withdrawal from occupied southern Lebanese positions — neither of which has occurred. The Beqaa Valley weapons site strike targets Hezbollah's production and storage infrastructure that the IDF says has been rebuilding since the April 8 ceasefire. Lebanon's cumulative toll since March 2: 3,073+ killed, 9,100+ wounded, 1.6M displaced.

media.caption: Day 85: IDF strikes Hezbollah underground weapons site in Beqaa Valley; Lebanese army soldier wounded near Nabatieh; Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension continues to fray
